$description: Color palette for the 'adminlte-classic' template (Classic Admin). Values obtained by observing the public visual identity of the AdminLTE project (ColorlibHQ) — see ATTRIBUTION.md. This is an original document, not an AdminLTE file.

primary.$description: Primary action color: main buttons, links, active navigation items, focus rings on interactive elements.

secondary.$description: Secondary/neutral action color: secondary buttons, medium-emphasis supporting text.

light.$description: Light neutral: subtle backgrounds, table row hover, section dividers.

dark.$description: Dark neutral: high-contrast text, background of dark chrome elements (e.g. sidebar).

canvas.$description: Default background of content surfaces: cards, tables, panels.

muted.$description: Background of the content area behind cards/panels — a light blue-gray that separates the card surface from the rest of the page.

border.$description: Default color for borders and dividers between surface elements.

primary.$description: Default body text, on light backgrounds.

inverse.$description: Text on dark backgrounds or on top of the primary color.

link.$description: Default color for text links, same as the primary color.

on-accent.$description: Text and icons placed directly on top of a saturated accent fill. Use ONLY over accents dark enough to carry white text at 4.5:1 or better: brand.primary (4.50:1), brand.secondary (4.69:1), status.success (4.53:1), status.danger (4.53:1), neutral.dark (15.43:1). Over any other fill use text.on-accent-dark.

on-accent-dark.$description: Text and icons placed directly on top of a LIGHT accent fill, where text.on-accent would fail WCAG AA. Required over status.warning (white is only 1.63:1; this token is 9.46:1), status.info (white is 1.96:1; this token is 7.88:1) and neutral.light (14.63:1). Every filled-surface component (Stat Callout, Badge, Alert, Button) must pick between this token and text.on-accent based on the accent it renders on — never default to white.

accent.$description: The accent colours darkened just enough to be legible AS TEXT on a light surface. Use these — never the raw brand/status value — whenever an accent colour is applied to text, an icon, or a 1px border on surface.canvas, surface.muted or neutral.light: an outline or link Button, a Subtle Badge, a tinted Alert's lead-in, a chart label. The raw accents are fills, and four of the six fall below 4.5:1 as text on the page background; status.warning is 1.63:1 and status.info 1.96:1 on white, which is not a near miss. Each value below clears 4.5:1 against all three light surfaces, verified against the darkest of them (surface.muted).

primary.$description: brand.primary as text. 4.99:1 on surface.canvas, 4.61:1 on surface.muted.

secondary.$description: brand.secondary as text. 5.03:1 on surface.canvas, 4.64:1 on surface.muted.

success.$description: status.success as text. 5.01:1 on surface.canvas, 4.63:1 on surface.muted.

danger.$description: status.danger as text. 4.99:1 on surface.canvas, 4.61:1 on surface.muted.

warning.$description: status.warning as text. The raw #ffc107 is 1.63:1 on white and unusable for text at any size; this is 4.99:1 on surface.canvas, 4.61:1 on surface.muted.

info.$description: status.info as text. The raw #0dcaf0 is 1.96:1 on white; this is 5.00:1 on surface.canvas, 4.61:1 on surface.muted.

sidebar-bg.$description: Background of the dark side navigation — a signature trait of the classic 'admin dashboard' look.

sidebar-text.$description: Default text color of side navigation items, at rest, on the dark background.

sidebar-text-active.$description: Text color of the side navigation item on hover, focus, or active state.

sidebar-item-hover-bg.$description: Background of a side navigation item on hover — a translucent white overlay on top of the dark background, the same pattern used for the active state.

sidebar-item-active-bg.$description: Background of the selected/active side navigation item.

topbar-bg.$description: Background of the top bar (topbar) — light, contrasting with the dark sidebar.

series-1.$description: First data series in a chart. Matches brand.primary so the dominant series reads as the page's primary accent.

series-2.$description: Second data series — a teal that separates from series-1 in hue and lightness. Measured, the three series clear colour-vision separation (worst adjacent pair, series-2 vs series-3, is deltaE 12.7 under deuteranopia), but series-2 sits at only 2.07:1 against a light chart surface — below the 3:1 a mark needs to carry identity on its own. Colour is therefore never the only way series are told apart: two or more series require a legend plus a per-series mark shape or dash, and the data-table equivalent specs/trend-chart-card.md mandates.

series-3.$description: Third data series — a warm orange, reserved for charts that genuinely need a third line. 2.5:1 against a light chart surface, so it carries the same legend-and-label obligation as series-2. Assign the three in fixed order and keep a given measure on the same colour across every chart; prefer splitting into two charts over adding a fourth series.

grid.$description: Axis lines, gridlines and tick marks inside a chart canvas. Same value as surface.border so chart chrome recedes to the same weight as the surrounding surface dividers.

sparkline.$description: Line and fill color of a compact sparkline that carries no axes or legend. Deliberately muted (matches text.secondary) so a strip of sparklines reads as supporting detail rather than competing with the primary chart on the same page.

backdrop.$description: Dimming layer painted behind a modal, offcanvas panel, or off-canvas sidebar. Built from neutral.dark at 50% opacity so page content stays faintly readable while clearly demoted; the overlay surface itself sits on surface.canvas above it.

accent-shade.$description: Darkening wash laid over a surface that is already filled with an accent colour, to separate a sub-area from the fill without introducing a second hue — e.g. a Stat Callout's footer strip, or the hover state of a control sitting on a filled surface. Works over both dark and light accents; never used on an unfilled (surface.canvas) background, where surface.border or neutral.light applies instead.

accent-glyph.$description: Colour of an oversized DECORATIVE glyph sitting on a dark accent fill (brand.primary, brand.secondary, status.success, status.danger). Deliberately low-contrast: this is background texture, not content, and must be aria-hidden. Never use it for a glyph that carries meaning — that one takes text.on-accent.

accent-glyph-dark.$description: The accent-glyph counterpart for LIGHT accent fills (status.warning, status.info, neutral.light), where a white glyph would be invisible. Same rule: decorative only, aria-hidden, never load-bearing.
